scope: Independent source derivation and public-input review; existing scientific and local-control reports inspected. No new numerical science or model evaluation run by reviewer.
findings: The finite-mass Langevin model, one velocity degree of freedom, stationary joint preparation, local Stratonovich bath calorimetry, centered variance and long-time-before-small-mass order uniquely define the measured rates.

The source has correct positional generator T/gamma times the second derivative, stationary density proportional to 1/T, exact mean entropy production and exact conditional-mean occupation variance. Its remaining physical approximation drops the independent entropy martingale, rather than corrupting positional stochastic calculus or the Poisson solve.

The one-cell Fourier coordinate correctly includes wavenumber in both temperature gradients and the diffusion generator. Centering with the stationary density and excluding the zero Fourier mode solve the correct periodic Poisson problem.

The oracle adds 2 times the mean entropy rate, which is the expected conditional martingale variance. The martingale has zero conditional mean given the entire position path, so no omitted cross term is required.

The reference independently solves the finite-mass Fourier/Hermite Kramers stationary and Poisson equations for the cubic heat functional. The kinetic and log-temperature endpoint terms have finite stationary second moments and do not alter these first two long-time cumulant rates. The mass scaling and extrapolation are consistent.
AUTHOR correctly restricts the fluctuation symmetry to the limiting anomalous functional; it does not claim an unrestricted exponential-moment domain for bare finite-mass bath entropy.

The exact neutral instruction allows replacement of all model code. Public source has unfinished fitting, no unused corrective imports, no hidden solver mandate and no reduced correction formula in the apparatus. Fixed sigma=0.0001 has no fitted-parameter dependence; public and private calibration copies match.
This is explicitly an entropy-anomaly family revision. Earlier outcomes remain historical and no evaluation difficulty claim is made for the new stage.
